subject: Reservation SKU eligibility and stress-scenario collaboration for Dedicated capacity
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir.rao@falconhealth.com>

Cc: procurement@falconhealth.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Reservation SKU eligibility + stress scenarios for Dedicated capacity

Hi Irene / Ben,

Thanks again for the overview last week. As part of Falcon Health's procurement process we're consolidating the answers to a couple of detailed questions to finalize the reservation commitment. Can you confirm the following items and provide any supporting artifacts?

1) SKU eligibility: which Reserved SKUs (GPU families / instance classes) are eligible for a committed pool versus a burst lane? We need to know which SKUs are subject to guaranteed throughput and which we should expect throttled burst behaviour on.

2) Tail-latency stress scenarios: we have a set of morning/pandemic surge and end-of-quarter concurrency spikes. Can you share a short stress-test plan and the commands/parameters you recommend so our infra team can reproduce tail-latency numbers in our environment?

3) Fallback policies: if a reserved SKU is unavailable (hardware maintenance or regional depletion), what automatic fallbacks does Redwood apply and how are throughput/SLOs impacted?

We'd appreciate a simple matrix showing SKU -> eligibility -> expected baseline throughput (tokens/sec or rps) and a sample stress test runbook. If you can attach a worksheet, that would be perfect.

Goal: finalize the reservation appendix by Friday 8/20.

Thanks,
Samir Rao

Falcon Health

Irene / Karthik / Samir — attached are the files: reservation-sku-eligibility-matrix_v1.xlsx and gpu-fitment-recommendations.pdf. Short summary below.

Summary highlights:
- Reserved pool SKUs (Guaranteed): G1-32 (A100-like), G2-48 (H100-like) families are eligible for committed reservation. These cover predictable throughput with pinned capacity. Expected baseline throughput per node (model family median, 1024-token context): G1-32 ~ 1.6k tokens/sec, G2-48 ~ 3.8k tokens/sec.
- Burst lane SKUs (Best-effort): T4-16 and Q8-variations are offered as burst lanes with up to +40% throughput for short windows, subject to regional availability. They are not part of SLA guarantees.
- Fallback policy: automatic routing to compatible SKUs in adjacent pool first (same region), then cross-region fallback if policy allows. Fallback reduces guaranteed throughput proportionally; we provide expected degradation percentages per SKU in the attached matrix.
- Packing & contention: at >75% pool utilization, tail-latency risk increases — we recommend a buffer band (10–15% of committed capacity) for critical workloads.

Stress-test plan (high-level):
- We recommend two reproducer profiles: steady-state peak (sustained 60–90 min at 80% concurrency) and spikemix (sudden 3x concurrency for 5–10 min).
- Included file stress-test-plan-commands.txt has the commands we use internally (load generator, sequence length, concurrency ramp, and a sample KV-cache warmup).

Next steps: Irene to add runbook language for the procurement appendix; Karthik to validate degradation numbers against current fleet.

Ben Carter
Senior Product Ops, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
Attachment: reservation-sku-eligibility-matrix_v1.xlsx; gpu-fitment-recommendations.pdf; stress-test-plan-commands.txt

Thanks Ben — this looks useful. A couple of clarifying Qs before we move it into the legal appendix:

- The throughput numbers look model-family dependent. Can you confirm the measurement model and tokenization? (We run a mix of code + clinical notes; we'd like to verify which baseline to use.)
- For cross-region fallback: do the latency SLOs change or only throughput? Our compliance team flagged cross-region fallbacks for some PHI-handling workloads.
- On stress tests: our infra team prefers Docker-based reproducer scripts; can you package the commands into a container recipe or give a quick Dockerfile snippet?

We can provision a short window next Tuesday 8/18 09:00–11:00 PT for a joint run if that works for Redwood — would like an on-call person to be present.

Samir

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reservation SKU eligibility + stress scenarios for Dedicated capacity

Samir — thanks for the follow-ups. Answers below and next steps.

1) Measurement model and tokenization: Baseline numbers in the matrix were measured using the "redwood-eval-std" harness (GPT-derivative, 8k context truncated to 1k for throughput tests) with byte-pair tokenization. For mixed workloads (code + clinical notes) we recommend using your representative prompt corpus and running the reproducer once; I'll include instructions in the runbook.

2) Cross-region fallback & SLOs: fallback primarily affects throughput, not the token-level correctness. However, p95/p99 latency will increase depending on inter-region RTT. For PHI workloads we recommend keeping a dedicated regional pool (we can flag SKUs as region-locked in the reservation appendix). Legal/Compliance note: cross-region routing can be disabled per reservation if required; we'll call that out clearly in the appendix.

3) Docker recipe: attached is a minimal Dockerfile snippet in the runbook and a short Makefile target for starting the reproducer. If you prefer, Mina (copied) can help convert the commands into a full container image and push to your registry prior to the scheduled test.

Jumping on the proposed slot Tue 8/18 09:00–11:00 PT — Ben will be on-call for fitment/fallback questions, Mina will run the reproducer, and Karthik will observe capacity counters. Please confirm attendees and we will send a calendar invite + a DocuSign link for the reservation appendix by Monday.

Action items:
- Falcon: confirm attendees for 8/18 window and whether cross-region fallback is acceptable for non-PHI workloads.
- Redwood: finalize appendix language, package Docker reproducer, send invite + DocuSign link (Irene).

Best,
Irene Choi
